claims.text: TiH2 and ZrH2 hydride precursors can be used in powder extrusion to produce Group-IV-containing refractory high-entropy alloys.
Processing under ultra-high vacuum below 10^-6 Pa or Ar containing less than 10 ppm O2 is sufficient to control oxygen uptake.
Holding at 400-600 °C for 30-60 minutes decomposes the hydride precursors and releases hydrogen.
The 400-600 °C degassing stage avoids premature oxidation and alpha-HCP precipitation.
Extrusion at 1100-1300 °C with heating faster than 50 °C/min bypasses the kinetic window for alpha-HCP nucleation.
A hydrostatic pressure of 100-200 MPa suppresses void formation during extrusion.
Cooling faster than 100 °C/min stabilizes a metastable BCC solid solution.
Rapid cooling prevents nucleation of brittle alpha-HCP phases.
Rapid cooling avoids miscibility-gap-driven precipitation of Al-Zr-rich or Ti-O-rich intermetallics.
Rapid removal of hydrogen and oxygen during degassing prevents brittle oxide inclusions and alpha-HCP precipitation.
Oxide inclusions and alpha-HCP phases raise the ductile-to-brittle transition temperature.
The starting powder should contain less than 500 ppm oxygen and be ball-milled under an inert atmosphere.
A degassing-plus-pressure-assisted powder process can produce a bulk material with greater than 98% relative density.
The proposed process produces a dense RHEA bulk form without catastrophic cracking.
The proposed process lowers DBTT by more than 100 °C relative to conventionally processed alloys.
The proposed process increases high-temperature yield strength by 20-30%.
The yield-strength improvement arises from solid-solution hardening and suppression of brittle phases.
BCC/B2 microstructures in a Ti- and Zr-containing RHEA are unstable during prolonged elevated-temperature exposure and develop extensive hexagonal precipitation.
Conventionally processed Group-IV-containing RHEAs exhibit oxygen-induced embrittlement, alpha-HCP precipitation, and elevated DBTT because of slow cooling and inadequate oxygen control.
The process is applicable broadly to Ti-, Zr-, or Hf-containing RHEAs with Nb, Ta, Mo, W, or V, but not to systems requiring liquid-phase sintering.

contradictions.description: The mechanism predicts that elevated oxygen or slower cooling should cause alpha-HCP formation and increased DBTT, but the falsification experiment says observing those expected effects under deliberately degraded conditions would falsify the hypothesis. Such a result would instead support the proposed dependence on oxygen and cooling rate; the decisive test should compare the nominal process against controls and fail the hypothesis if the nominal process does not suppress these outcomes.
